AJITHKUMAR, JJ. ----------------------------------------------------- DBP No.81 of 2024 ------------------------------------------------------ Dated this the 13th day of September, 2024 ORDER Anil K. Narendran, J. According to 'Agama Sastra' Hindu temples represent the culmination of social and religious aspirations of a society. The temple is the focal point in the life of a community and often represents its pride, identity and unity. It draws into its fold people from its various segments and denominations and binds them together. The worship that takes place in the sanctum sanctorum and within the temple premises is important; so are the festivals and occasional processions that involve the direct participation of the entire community. They complement each other. While the worship of the deity in the sanctum sanctorum might be an individual's spiritual or religious need; the festivals are the expression of a community's joy, exuberance, devotion and pride and are also an idiom of a community's cohesiveness. 2. This DBP is registered suo motu vide order dated 26.07.2024 in DBP No.57 of 2022 and W.P.(C)No.22489 of 2024, after obtaining the order of the Hon'ble the Acting Chief Justice, on the conduct of 'Kodi Archana' and 'Vadakkupurathu Pattu' in Vaikom Sree Mahadeva Temple, which are scheduled to be conducted from 17.03.2025 for 41 days and 01.04.2025 to 13.04.2025, respectively. Report No.2 of 2024 in DBP No.57 of 2022 filed by the learned Advocate Commissioner forms part of this DBP. 3. On 01.08.2024, when this DBP came up for consideration, the learned Senior Government Pleader entered appearance for respondents 1 to 8; Adv.A. Sreekala, the learned Standing Counsel for Vaikom Municipality for the 9th respondent and the learned Standing Counsel for Travancore Devaswom Board for respondents 10 to 14.
texts.facts: By the order dated 06.09.2024, the learned Standing Counsel for Travancore Devaswom Board was directed to make available for the perusal of this Court the files relating to the decision taken by the Devaswom Commissioner. Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950 enacted by the State Legislature makes provision for the administration, supervision and control of incorporated and unincorporated Devaswoms and of other Hindu Religious Endowments and Funds. One post of Vice President is lying vacant since, in the order of approval granted by the Temple Advisory Committee, approval was not granted in the case of a persons, who is the Secretary of Sree Vaikathappan Annadhana Trust, on account of a pending litigation with the Travancore Devaswom Board. 14. Having considered the submissions made at the Bar, we are of the view that instead of the person holding the post of Municipal Vice Chairman, Vaikom Municipality, who is otherwise engaged in official works, the 50 member Committee can elect an office bearer/member of the Temple Advisory Committee as Vice President. In another post of Vice President as well an office bearer/member of the Temple Advisory Committee can be elected by the 50 member Committee. 15. Out of 15 persons elected as Secretaries of various committees, two persons are members of the Temple Advisory Committee. Considering the nature of responsibilities of various Committees, we are of the view that the 50 member Committee can elect the an office bearer/member of the Temple Advisory Committee, either as Secretary or Convenor of Finance Committee, Counter 1 and Counter 2 and Food and Accommodation Committee.
